name: Ladder: LevelInfoChanged
summary: LevelInfoChangedMsg, the rung from WaitingForSpawnPoint (16) to WaitingForPlayerSpawn (17). Handler decompiled on build 30fe6461 and the 106-byte BODY parsed end to end from the 1.365 replay (110 bytes including the 4-byte typed header).
purpose: Tell the client which level to load and which client context instance it belongs to, then let it wait for the player spawn.

created_when: the client has identified itself and is waiting for a spawn point
lifecycle.if_absent: the map never loads and the client never reaches WaitingForPlayerSpawn

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the prefix varint a3 19 = 1635 = 0x663. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 110-byte record starts 4 bytes earlier.

fields.name: level_name
fields.note: Length byte then characters. Measured: 0x14 followed by 'NewWorld_VitaeEterna'.

fields.name: level_path
fields.note: Length byte then characters. Measured: 0x1e followed by 'coatlicue/NewWorld_VitaeEterna'.

fields.name: level_bounds
fields.note: Four big-endian floats: 2048.0, 16.0, 12272.0, 10250.0 on the measured record. Measured live 2026-10-26: the decoded struct holds the same four values and its verbatim copy proves the big-endian reading (FUN_146447ac0). The wire carries no count prefix, so the literal count 4 fixes the run.

fields.name: unresolved_u64
fields.note: Measured zero, 8 bytes. The handler never reads it and no second signal names it, so the meaning stays unnamed; the width is stated by the atlas, so the shape is carried as u64be.

fields.name: unresolved_u32
fields.note: Measured 01 01 00 00, 4 bytes. The atlas states it is NOT a be_f32 and NOT the struct's four u8 (those are the four bytes at body 0x5e); which struct slot it reaches is unmeasured. Carried as u32be; big-endian follows the repo rule for fixed-width wire integers and the endianness itself is not measured.

fields.name: session_nonce
fields.note: Measured 9c fa 58 61 78 14 69 f2. Upgraded from candidate to verified on 2026-10-25: the SAME 8-byte value appears in the periodic counter message 0x18a6 at offset 0x18, after the same four flag bytes 01 01 00 00 and before the same six bytes 65 03 00 00 00 00. Two different message types carrying one value is stronger than any single record's layout, and the value differs per session rather than per record. Big-endian inferred from the repo rule that fixed-width wire integers are big-endian; the endianness itself is not measured.

fields.name: unresolved_group
fields.note: Measured 65 03 00 00 00 00 01 01 01 00, 10 bytes. The atlas splits it: six unnamed bytes then the four u8 the struct calls +0xa0..+0xa3 (01 01 01 00). Not read by the handler. The size (10) is stated, so the shape is carried as bytes(10); the meaning stays unknown. meanings.md '`0x663` laid out to the byte'.

fields.name: level_context_key
fields.note: The last 8 bytes of the body, measured 00 00 00 c1 7f 9b e4 8f. The handler compares it against the component slot it cached last time and RETURNS EARLY when they match, then stores the new value. So it is the dedup key: a repeated LevelInfo with the same key is ignored by the client. This is a second, independent signal for the same fact the lab had already recorded from the capture (the repeated seq 0x663 at 0x4d carries the same key and is ignored).

evidence.ref: handler FUN_146447ac0, .pdata 0x146447ac0-0x146447f4f (1167 bytes) on build 30fe6461f929ba44178376a72f0765dc5da28ccba20e5006a60a229babd74033. Reached as a virtual method through the adjustor thunk 0x146447aa8 in vtable slot 0x1484fdb88, the slot right after the self-identification handler

the handler reads only three struct offsets: +0xa1 (the value it logs as levelInfo.m_clientContextInstanceId), +0xa2, and +0xa8 (compared against the cached component slot -0x7f8 with an early return). Everything else in the struct is filled by the deserializer and never touched here

five format strings, all lea-referenced only from FUN_146447ac0: 0x148500d28 'LevelInfoChanged', 0x148500d40 '... failed - pGame is nullptr', 0x148500d70 '... m_clientContextInstanceId %d changing to levelInfo.m_clientContextInstanceId %d', 0x148500dd8 '... javContext.IsMasterPlayer is false', 0x148500e10 '... m_reloadLevel is false'

services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt record 0x10_T0x663_R.bin, 110 bytes including the 4-byte typed header, 106-byte body, parsed end to end: 14+'NewWorld_VitaeEterna', 1e+'coatlicue/NewWorld_VitaeEterna', four BE floats at body 0x34, u64 zero at body 0x44, 01 01 00 00 at body 0x4c, the nonce at body 0x50, 65 03 00 00 00 00 01 01 01 00 at body 0x58, and the key at body 0x62

FUN_146403a70 (0x146403a70-0x146403b58, 232 bytes) is the copy constructor the handler calls first: it initialises two std::strings (FUN_1402b0720 at +0x00 and +0x28), copies 4 x u32 at +0x50, a u64 at +0x60, a 56-byte sub-object at +0x68 through FUN_141608020, then the bytes at +0xa0, +0xa1, +0xa2, +0xa3 and the u64 at +0xa8. That enumeration is the struct layout, and it is why +0xa8 is the last member

the decoded LevelInfo struct member list (was this card's former where:'memory' fields[]) is: std::string at +0x00, u64 at +0x20, std::string at +0x28, u64 at +0x48, 4 x f32 at +0x50, u64 at +0x60, a 56-byte sub-object at +0x68 copied by FUN_141608020, then the bytes at +0xa0, +0xa1 (m_clientContextInstanceId), +0xa2, +0xa3 and the u64 at +0xa8. It is a decoded struct, not the wire body, so it is recorded here rather than in fields[]
FUN_146411a10 (619 bytes) is the matching assignment into the component at param_1-0x8b0; it writes the same offsets, which is a second confirmation of the member list

the same key value is pinned independently in services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/replay_store.py as REPLAY_CAPTURED_LEVELINFO_KEY = 000000c17f9be48f, with a comment that the duplicate with the same key is ignored by the client-side dedup check

cross-message confirmation of the tail envelope: the level-info tail is [01 01 00 00][session nonce][65 03 00 00 00 00][discriminator], and the periodic counter message 0x18a6 carries the identical first three components at its own 0x14/0x18/0x20 before its own discriminator 02 and counter byte
